definition: Hypothesis Testing is a core concept in Data Science. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Hypothesis Testing is
theory.body: Hypothesis Testing describes the methods and patterns used within Data Science to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Hypothesis Testing is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Hypothesis Testing matters
theory.body: Without Hypothesis Testing, systems built with Data Science are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Hypothesis Testing works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Hypothesis Testing follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Hypothesis Testing.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Hypothesis Testing
theory.body: Hypothesis Testing offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
